Forwarding chargeback notice from Acme (attached). Key facts: original invoice 2027-11-15, settled by card on 2027-11-20, bank chargeback posted 2027-12-09. Amount $38,450. Acme asking for evidence or a credit memo.

Questions for finance:
- Do we have a bank trace showing the settlement? (I have a copy from their side but want Redwoods' posting)
- Operationally, should we create a credit memo to offset AR or post a reversing revenue JE this period? Impact to revenue recognition is the tricky part since the original revenue was recognized in Nov month-end.
- There's potential FX timing: customer paid in EUR originally and chargeback was processed after month close — do we keep original FX reval entries?

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 13 Dec 2027 10:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Chargeback Notice: INV-2042

Jordan — thanks for the ping and attaching the Acme notice. Quick summary from AR side after a first pass:

- Our AR ledger shows INV-2042 closed (payment applied) on 2027-11-20. The bank batch shows a debit on 2027-12-09 for the card chargeback.
- We can either (A) post a credit memo and reduce AR and leave revenue as-is (would require revenue erosion on next period as a contra if we don't reverse now), or (B) post a reversing JE to reduce revenue in Dec and adjust AR to match the bank chargeback immediately.

Given Acme is requesting proof to dispute, if we can provide a bank trace and evidence of delivery we might win the dispute and avoid any accounting entries. If dispute is unsuccessful or Acme requests a credit, option B (revenue reversing JE dated 2027-12-09) is preferred for matching purposes so P&L reflects the cash movement in the period it occurred.

FX: I checked — the invoice was billed in EUR but our functional currency is USD. The original settlement hit USD on 2027-11-20 based on that day's rate; the chargeback settled later and the bank's USD / EUR rate differs. We will need to run an FX revaluation for Nov and Dec to present correct realized FX. If we reverse revenue in Dec, we should use the chargeback date rate for the reversal and book realized FX to finance P&L.

I will prepare a proposed journal (Marcus, see attached draft request) and mark AR for a chargeback hold to prevent automated collections from reopening the invoice.

Grace
Director, Accounts Receivable

Adding proposed JE and GL treatment. High-level suggested entries if we proceed with revenue reversal (Option B):

1) Reverse recognized revenue (use revenue account 4000)
   Dr Revenue 4000: $38,450
   Cr Revenue Reversal clearing (temporary) 4099: $38,450

2) Post AR movement to clear the chargeback against customer balance
   Dr Customer Chargeback Expense 6500 (or contra-rev if policy dictates): $38,450
   Cr Accounts Receivable - Acme 1200: $38,450

3) Realized FX differences (if any) to FX Gain/Loss 7600 — calculate based on bank trace rate on 2027-12-09 vs original settlement rate.

Operational notes:
- Date for JE: 2027-12-09 to align with bank posting.
- We should create a memo line pointing to Acme chargeback file HBSP-52341 to support audit.
- Lauren, please confirm whether we should use chargeback expense or treat it as contra-revenue per policy for revenue reporting — treatment affects SaaS bookings reporting.

I attached a draft JE workbook with sample FX calculation. If approved, I'll route for AP/GL posting and include supporting attachments.

Marcus Lin
Manager, Financial Controls
